Smith Land Management is Troy Smith's business in Marshfield, Wisconsin. He handles the heavy work outside, from a new gravel drive to rock that's too big to shift by hand.

What Troy does

Gravel driveways

Built with a crown, so rain sheds off to the sides. That's usually what keeps a gravel drive from rutting and holding puddles.

Ponds

Dug and shaped to fit the spot. Tell Troy what you picture and he'll look at the ground with you.

Rock walls and heavy rocks

Fieldstone walls set by machine, and big rocks moved where you want them or out of the way.

Food plots

Ground opened up and worked for a food plot on your land.

Paths through woods or over a hill

A trail cleared where you want one on your property.

Digging and burying

Holes dug and things buried. Tell Troy what it is and where it needs to go.

    Gravel driveways

    Built with a crown.

    A crown is a gentle hump down the middle of the drive. Rain runs off it to the sides and drains away.

    A flat drive holds the water instead, and that's usually where the ruts and soft spots start. Flip between the two and watch where the rain goes.
